name: AI APIs and Integrations
blurb: Endpoints, SDKs, authentication, rate limits, pricing, uptime, and changelogs for every public AI API.

reading.body:
AI APIs and integrations are split into four reference layers: a directory of public APIs, pricing and rate limits, status and uptime history, and the serving providers that run inference.

The top level contains no direct records; all content lives in those four child directories. That split separates the technical surface of an API from its commercial terms and its operational reliability, which are the three things a production AI integration actually depends on.

The serving provider directory adds a governance dimension. It lists over 100 providers with headquarters country and datacenter regions, because those jurisdictions determine which AI regulations, data residency rules, and export controls apply to a deployment. It is sourced daily from the OpenRouter routing catalog, so it reflects current routing rather than a static snapshot.

What the data does not show is any aggregate metric or direct comparison across providers. It also does not include compute capacity or power consumption, only datacenter regions as a jurisdictional and operational anchor.
